precepts.text: The parallel account states plainly that they put away the strange wives together with the children born of them.
precepts.point: All these had taken strange wives, and some of them had wives by whom they had children, so that some put away only the wives and some the wives and children born of them.

note.label: Ezra 10: The Covenant to Put Away Strange Wives

precepts.why:
Ezra ends the roll with the words “All these had taken strange wives: and some of them had wives by whom they had children.” The parallel account in 1 Esdras says plainly what was done about those children: “All these had taken strange wives, and they put them away with their children.”

So the covenant was kept to the full. Some put away only the wives; those who had children by them put away the wives and the children born of them. The sons of Jeshua the son of Jozadak had given their hands to put away their wives, and being guilty they “offered a ram of the flock for their trespass”; the Levites, the singers, the porters and the men of Israel by their families are named after them, a long roll of those who had transgressed in this thing, and the strange wives and their children went out from all of them.

precepts.text: After the sin was dealt with, the multitude gathered and asked Ezra the reader to bring the law of Moses, showing Ezra came also to teach the people the law.
precepts.point: All these had taken strange wives, and some of them had wives by whom they had children, so that some put away only the wives and some the wives and children born of them.

note.label: Ezra 10: The Covenant to Put Away Strange Wives

precepts.why:
Once the sin was dealt with and the strange wives put away, the priests, the Levites and they that were of Israel “dwelt in Jerusalem, and in the country, in the first day of the seventh month: so the children of Israel were in their habitations.”

Then “the whole multitude came together with one accord into the broad place of the holy porch toward the east”, and they asked “Esdras the priest and reader, that he would bring the law of Moses, that was given of the Lord God of Israel.” Ezra brought the law “unto the whole multitude from man to woman, and to all the priests, to hear law in the first day of the seventh month.”

That is why Ezra came: not only to put away the trespass of the strange wives, but to teach the people the law. The roll of names in Ezra 10 is the cleansing; what follows is the whole multitude, men and women, gathered with one accord to hear the law of Moses.

precepts.text: Ezra read the law from morning until midday, and stood upon a pulpit of wood made for that purpose, the same order followed at camp with a reader and a pulpit.
precepts.point: All these had taken strange wives, and some of them had wives by whom they had children, so that some put away only the wives and some the wives and children born of them.

note.label: Ezra 10: The Covenant to Put Away Strange Wives

precepts.why:
Ezra “read in the broad court before the holy porch from morning unto midday, before both men and women; and the multitude gave heed unto the law.” Then “Esdras the priest and reader of the law stood up upon a pulpit of wood, which was made for that purpose.”

This is the order kept at camp today: a reader and a pulpit, the law read before men and women together, and the multitude giving heed. The people who had just put away their strange wives and their children were the same people who now stood from morning until midday to hear the law, the reader standing on a pulpit of wood made for that purpose.

precepts.text: When Ezra opened the law the people stood straight up, he blessed the Most High, and all the people answered Amen, lifted their hands, and fell to the earth to worship, the same order kept in the classes today.
precepts.point: All these had taken strange wives, and some of them had wives by whom they had children, so that some put away only the wives and some the wives and children born of them.

note.label: Ezra 10: The Covenant to Put Away Strange Wives

precepts.why:
“And when he opened the law, they stood all straight up. So Esdras blessed the Lord God most High, the God of hosts, Almighty. And all the people answered, Amen; and lifting up their hands they fell to the ground, and worshipped the Lord.”

When the law was opened the people stood straight up; Ezra blessed the Most High; all the people answered Amen, lifted their hands, and fell to the earth to worship. That is the same order kept in the classes today. After the trespass of the strange wives was put away, this is where the people of Ezra 10 were brought: standing for the opening of the law, answering Amen, and worshipping the Lord.

points: Esdras, rising from the court of the temple, went to the chamber of Joanan the son of Eliasib, and remained there, and did eat no meat nor drink water, mourning for the great iniquities of the multitude.

points: There was a proclamation in all Jewry and Jerusalem to all them that were of the captivity, that they should be gathered together at Jerusalem.

note.label: 1 Esdras 9: The Strange Wives Put Away and the Law Read to the People

points: In three days were all they of the tribe of Judah and Benjamin gathered together at Jerusalem, the twentieth day of the ninth month; and all the multitude sat trembling in the broad court of the temple because of the present foul weather.

note.label: 1 Esdras 9: The Strange Wives Put Away and the Law Read to the People

points: Esdras arose up and said unto them, Ye have transgressed the law in marrying strange wives, thereby to increase the sins of Israel. Now by confessing give glory unto the Lord God of our fathers, and do his will, and separate yourselves from the heathen of the land, and from the strange women.

note.label: 1 Esdras 9: The Strange Wives Put Away and the Law Read to the People

points: The whole multitude cried and said with a loud voice, Like as thou hast spoken, so will we do.

note.label: 1 Esdras 9: The Strange Wives Put Away and the Law Read to the People

points: But forasmuch as the people are many, and it is foul weather, and this is not a work of a day or two, let the rulers of the multitude stay, and let all them of our habitations that have strange wives come at the time appointed, with the rulers and judges of every place, till we turn away the wrath of the Lord from us for this matter.

note.label: 1 Esdras 9: The Strange Wives Put Away and the Law Read to the People

points: Esdras the priest chose unto him the principal men of their families, all by name; and in the first day of the tenth month they sat together to examine the matter, and their cause was brought to an end in the first day of the first month.

note.label: 1 Esdras 9: The Strange Wives Put Away and the Law Read to the People
